acceptance_4_residual_finding.finding: The collector republishes each RSS item as a new version every run (deploy/collector/collector_stack/pollers.py RssHubNewsPoller.collect stores ET.tostring(item_el) as raw_bytes; bundle.py hashes raw bytes as content_sha256; pipeline admits one job per source version). This task does not change the bundle hash. If the measurement shows pairs_input_digest_changed is near 0 (differences only outside the stored text), the collector should stop republishing unchanged items: hash only the fields that define the item (guid, title, description, pubDate) or skip an item whose normalized text equals the previous run's. If it shows text changes (for example description markup), the collector should normalize that markup before hashing. Either way L2 spend is already bounded here by one call per source and unchanged input.

decisions.acceptance_2_input_digest: hypothesis_card.extraction_input_digest hashes the rendered prompt (build_hypothesis_prompt of the truncated text, source_record_id, origin), the model schema and HYPOTHESIS_CARD_SCHEMA_VERSION plus EXTRACTION_INPUT_DIGEST_VERSION. Fetch time, run id, bundle hash and raw path never reach the model and are not in it. The ledger keeps one terminal answer per (source, input digest) in input_answers for card, no_hypothesis and rejected (the worker's hypothesis_rejected). A later version with the same digest reuses it with no call and no ledger event; its outbox skip reason names the earlier L2 event id ('no_hypothesis: reused L2 event N' or 'hypothesis_card_reused: L2 event N; card delivered by <job>'). A reused card whose earlier version was not delivered (no done version) is delivered by the new version, so a card is never lost. A changed input has a new digest and is extracted.
decisions.acceptance_2_l2_irrelevant: l2_irrelevant is decided before any call from title and metadata as well as the text, at no cost, so it is decided again per version and never stored as a reusable answer. failed and unavailable are never reused.
decisions.acceptance_2_limits_per_source: record_attempts rows are summed per source (reads sum every row of the source; new calls write the digest '' row). Existing per-digest rows keep counting until the 30-day prune. Limits stay 3 a day and 6 in total, now per source. ExtractionLedger.reserve_attempt/can_attempt/record_attempts keep their signatures; digest is ignored.
decisions.acceptance_2_defect_reattempt: A row stamped defect_reattempted=1 is extracted with reuse_answers=False, so its one call is made even when an answer for the same input exists; it still counts against the per-source limits and daily cap.
decisions.acceptance_3_supersede: On admission of a new version (inside the insert transaction) older versions of the source in pending or retry_wait are closed skipped 'superseded_by_newer_version: <newer job id>' and never called. Backlog admitted before the switch is closed the same way by claim_due. A version leased by another worker is closed by begin_job (before the attempt is counted and before any call) with DistillationSupersededError; a version already started finishes and its answer is reused by the newer one. The newest version is the only eligible one.
decisions.acceptance_5_probe: The ledger calls row gains a sources column (distinct sources with a first call today) and summary() reports distinct_sources and calls_per_source (also in the controller tick's extraction summary). acceptance/discovery_pipeline_day.py hypothesis_cards stage reports distinct_sources and calls_per_source and fails above 1.5 (llm_calls_per_source_over_limit) when the BFF board carries llm_calls_today.distinct_sources; when it does not, the stage reports calls_per_source_status=distinct_sources_not_reported and does not fail on it. Plumbing the ledger value through discovery_summary.llm_calls and the BFF alpha_factory llm_calls_today (one additive key each) is outside the artifact contract and is a follow-up (commit cbb236784 holds a tested version).

runtime_budget.superseded_rows: No new row kinds: the 1,677 outbox, inbox and source-version rows per day (one per collector run per item) are still written; about 1,325 of them (versions beyond the first of each of 352 sources) are now closed superseded or reused instead of waiting and being paid for. Terminal rows and their payloads are removed by DistillationJobQueue.prune after DISTILLATION_QUEUE_TERMINAL_RETENTION_SECONDS (default 7 days).

state_rows_per_day.input_answers: at most one row per (source, input digest) with a paid terminal answer: at most the 211 answered calls seen today (about 78 sources) and bounded above by 352 sources per day, each detail <= 500 B plus a card JSON for cards only (a few KB, tens a day): well under 1.5 MB/day upper bound. Pruned at 30 days by put_input_answer (RECORD_ATTEMPT_RETENTION_DAYS) and kept alive by touch while versions keep arriving.
